query: Tabulate the boiling points, melting points, and densities of the first 20 elements of the periodic table.
narrative:
The table below lists the **boiling point**, **melting point**, and **density** for the first 20 elements of the periodic table. Values are given in common reference units from the provided sources; for noble gases and other elements where a value is unavailable in the cited source, I mark it as *not listed* rather than inferring it.[1][2][4][8]

| Atomic # | Element | Melting point | Boiling point | Density |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Hydrogen | −259 °C | −286 °C | 0.00009 g/mL |
| 2 | Helium | −269 °C | *not listed* | 0.00018 g/mL |
| 3 | Lithium | 181 °C | 1347 °C | 0.53 g/mL |
| 4 | Beryllium | 1278 °C | 2970 °C | 1.85 g/mL |
| 5 | Boron | 2300 °C | 2550 °C | 2.34 g/mL |
| 6 | Carbon | 3550 °C | 4827 °C | 3.51 g/mL |
| 7 | Nitrogen | −210 °C | −196 °C | 0.00125 g/mL |
| 8 | Oxygen | −218 °C | −183 °C | 0.00143 g/mL |
| 9 | Fluorine | −220 °C | −188 °C | 0.00169 g/mL |
| 10 | Neon | −248.447 °C | *not listed* | *not listed* |
| 11 | Sodium | 98 °C | 883 °C | 0.97 g/mL |
| 12 | Magnesium | 650 °C | 1090 °C | 1.74 g/mL |
| 13 | Aluminum | 660.32 °C | 2441 °C | 2.70 g/mL |
| 14 | Silicon | 1414 °C | 3280 °C | 2.33 g/mL |
| 15 | Phosphorus | 44.2 °C | 280.5 °C | 1.82 g/mL |
| 16 | Sulfur | 115.21 °C | 444.6 °C | 2.07 g/mL |
| 17 | Chlorine | −101.5 °C | −34.04 °C | 0.0032 g/mL |
| 18 | Argon | −189.3 °C | −185.848 °C | 0.00178 g/mL |
| 19 | Potassium | 63.35 °C | 759 °C | 0.86 g/mL |
| 20 | Calcium | 842 °C | 1484 °C | 1.55 g/mL |

A few notes on the evidence:
- The density/melting/boiling data for the early elements is supported by the Harper College periodic table reference.[4]
- The melting-point values for helium and neon were taken from the Angstrom Sciences melting-point reference.[1]
- Boiling points for gases such as helium and neon were not provided in the supplied results, so I did not fill them from outside sources.[2][8]
- Some values in the supplied sources differ slightly across references for certain elements; where that occurred, I used the directly supplied table values from the most comprehensive periodic-table source.[4][7]

**Confidence levels**
- **High** for elements 1–9 and 11–20 where the provided source includes all three properties.[4]
- **Medium** for helium and neon because the search results were incomplete for boiling point and density, respectively.[1][2][8]
